issues.current: 'Minimum 8 hours' (2015 placement-agency amendment, 'verify current'); the §245.71 training rule for direct-service agencies is described as 'not retrieved'; recruiting and onboarding cost is $30 per client-month
issues.correct: IDPH's current survey guidance says each home services agency must provide or arrange at least 10 hours of training per home services worker. The guidance also requires 10 total hours of training in each later year of employment, covering required annual topics. Older rule text (2010 amendment and secondary summaries) reads 8 hours: 4 before the first assignment and 4 within 30 days, plus 8 hours a year. Dementia training also applies to workers who serve dementia clients, reportedly 6 hours initial and 3 hours annual per a secondary source.
issues.evidence: IDPH guidance: "Each home services agency shall provide or arrange for a minimum of 10 hours of training for each home services worker."
issues.fix: Cite 77 IAC 245.71 as the controlling rule and state it as 10 initial hours plus 10 annual hours. Note that part of the initial training must come before the first assignment, and read §245.71 to confirm the split. Add a separate paid-training line: hours × wage × 1.19 burden × number of new hires per year. At about 25 part-time aides, that is roughly $5,000 or more a year for initial training alone, before turnover. Add Alzheimer's/dementia training costs. Delete the 8-hour figure, which comes from the placement-agency rule.

issues.current: Owner-administrator is the sole supervisor for 20 clients. Manager role cited to '77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(f)'. No alternate manager. No on-call coverage cost.
issues.correct: §245.40 requires a designated supervisor who is available to workers at all times (24/7). It also requires supervisory visits, including an annual on-site observation of each home services worker, plus agency supervisory visits. The IDPH application has an 'Alternate Agency Manager' line and sends manager qualifications to §245.30 ('245.30f'). The (f) subsection citation could not be verified. §245.40(a) is headed 'Home Health Administrator or Agency Manager.'

issues.fix: Change the cite to §245.40(a), §245.40(c) and §245.30 (unverified: confirm the exact subsection in the Part 245 text). Name an alternate manager or add an on-call stipend to the il_private20 configuration. Show that supervisory-visit labor, including one annual observed visit per worker, is covered in the 20-client plan (the owner-only model may not cover it).

issues.current: Benefits at 4% 'including paid leave'; 'verify paid-leave obligations locally'
issues.correct: Paid leave is mandatory and is not a verify-locally item. The statewide Paid Leave for All Workers Act (820 ILCS 192) accrues 1 hour per 40 worked, up to 40 hours a year. Chicago's ordinance (effective 7/1/2024) requires more for Chicago employees: paid leave plus paid sick leave, accruing 1 hour per 35 worked. At 4% total, accrual alone (2.5% statewide, higher in Chicago) leaves almost nothing for other benefits.
issues.evidence: unverifiable in this session. I did not fetch the statute or the City of Chicago ordinance. This comes from my knowledge of the law.
issues.fix: Add an explicit paid-leave accrual line. At least 2.5% of aide wages statewide. Use the Chicago accrual, and a payout of unused leave if the agency's policy provides one, for Chicago hires. Confirm both against the ILGA statute and Chicago's Office of Labor Standards. Raise benefits_pct above 4% or split it into statutory leave and other benefits.

Confirm Chicago against the Chicago Office of Labor Standards and Cook County against its own notice. The $17.21 wage clears all three, but by only $0.16 in Chicago.
